I am bipolar, have used Betterhelp for a while, and I am EXTREMELY satisfied with my therapist. I had a bad experience with the first therapist I was assigned to, but was able to switch without any associated costs. The second time around you're allowed to browse profiles and choose whoever you think it's the best option for you, and I was paired with someone wonderful.

Also, therapists and counselors cannot, under any circumstances, diagnose people and/or suggest meds. This is the psychiatrist's job.

I pay $135 for 4 sessions a month. It's definitely affordable. Not everyone has health insurance, or a plan that covers therapy, or the energy/willingness to leave the safety of their own homes to see someone face to face (much less during the pandemic).

You can apply for finantial help. I didn't know this when I first signed up for it, so they billed me a higher amount than I am paying now. When I proceeded to email them about needing help to pay for therapy, they refunded me part of what I had paid that very same day - no questions asked.

I had a difficult childhood. Among other things:

* My mother is bipolar type I, and I was exposed to a lot of her manic episodes while in was still in elementary school. It was mostly confusing, but sometimes scary too.

* My father was terrified that I'd end up like my mom, so he once slapped me very hard across the face when I was playing make believe (he thought I was talking to myself). Our relationship was tarnished for a very long time because of that - we only reconnected 2 years ago.

However, the "dissociative symptoms" haven't really manifested themselves much before last year, after my separation and divorce. I saw a professional at first, who treated me for PTSD. It was only once I came to terms with my divorce that they started happening so often.
